skills/toil/kibana.md

Status, spaces, dashboards, data views and alerting rules on Kibana, through its REST API. Every command reads; none changes anything. Verification level: unit.

Supported versions: The oldest Kibana version toil supports hasn’t been established. status reads both the 7.x (state/title) and the 8.x (level/summary) shapes; data-views list calls /api/data_views, which Kibana added in 8.0, so on 7.x it fails with NOT_FOUND. Requests follow Elastic’s current Kibana API reference. No release has been verified yet.

Credential

A Kibana or Elasticsearch API key: in Kibana, Stack Management → API keys → Create API key. Copy the encoded value, shown once when the key is created, and give it access to the Kibana features you’ll read (dashboards, data views, alerting). toil sends it as Authorization: ApiKey <encoded>, with kbn-xsrf: true, only to the connection’s baseUrl. There is no username, password or browser login.

Configuration

KeyEnv varRequiredMeaning
baseUrlTOIL_KIBANA_BASE_URLyesKibana root, e.g. https://kibana.imagile.dev (keep any context path, such as a basePath). Kibana itself, not Elasticsearch
apiKeyTOIL_KIBANA_API_KEYnoThe encoded API key. Unset, the paired Elasticsearch connection’s key is used (below)
spaceTOIL_KIBANA_SPACEnoDefault space id for the space-scoped commands; unset or default is the default space
apiKeyFromTOIL_KIBANA_API_KEY_FROMnoThe Elasticsearch connection whose apiKey this connection uses when it has none of its own

There’s no CI fallback variable.

Environment variables (CI, or a one-off shell):

export TOIL_KIBANA_BASE_URL=https://kibana.imagile.dev
export TOIL_KIBANA_API_KEY=<your encoded API key>
export TOIL_KIBANA_SPACE=ops   # optional

Or ~/.toil/config.json:

{
  "version": 2,
  "connections": {
    "kibana-prod": { "area": "kibana", "baseUrl": "https://kibana.imagile.dev", "space": "ops" }
  },
  "defaults": { "kibana": { "connection": "kibana-prod" } }
}

The key never goes in this file; a plaintext one there is refused with CONFIG_INVALID. Run toil connections add kibana-prod --area kibana (or toil connections login kibana-prod for an existing connection) to keep it in the OS credential store, or set TOIL_KIBANA_API_KEY.

Using the Elasticsearch key

One key often serves both. A Kibana connection uses an Elasticsearch connection’s apiKey only when you pair them, by naming that connection in apiKeyFrom:

{
  "version": 2,
  "connections": {
    "es-prod": { "area": "elasticsearch", "baseUrl": "https://elasticsearch.imagile.dev" },
    "kibana-prod": { "area": "kibana", "baseUrl": "https://kibana.imagile.dev", "apiKeyFrom": "es-prod" }
  }
}

An unpaired connection never gets another area’s key, with one exception, an env fallback the contract specifies: Kibana’s default connection takes TOIL_ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEY when TOIL_KIBANA_API_KEY isn’t set. Which key wins: an env value beats a stored one, and within a tier Kibana’s own key wins. The borrowed key is still sent only to Kibana’s baseUrl, never to Elasticsearch’s. meta.context.shared says when the key came from Elasticsearch (the connection, and env or store, never the value), and a 401 or 403 while sending it says so in the error: such a key may lack Kibana privileges, so give that Kibana connection its own key with toil connections login <name> (or TOIL_KIBANA_API_KEY for the default connection).

With no key at all, commands fail with NOT_CONFIGURED, naming both ways to set one.

Commands

--space <id> on dashboards, data-views and rules picks the space, falling back to the connection’s space; the default space has no URL prefix, any other is /s/<id>/api/.... Each of those commands reports space as the id used, or default. status and spaces list are never space-scoped.

  • status: Show Kibana version and overall status. data is { name, uuid, version, buildFlavor, status, summary }. An unhealthy Kibana answers 503 with its status in the body, and that’s a successful answer (status unavailable, say); a 503 without Kibana’s own status, such as a proxy’s, is an HTTP error.
  • spaces list: List the spaces the API key can see. data is { count, spaces }, each { id, name, description, disabledFeatures }.
  • dashboards list: List dashboards (id, title, description, last updated). --search matches titles (a trailing * is a wildcard). One page per call: --page (default 1) and --per-page (default 100), each a whole number of at least 1. data is { space, total, page, perPage, count, dashboards }; ask for the next page while page × perPage < total. Kibana marks the API it uses (_find) as deprecated, though it still serves it.
  • dashboards export: Export dashboards as saved objects, including the visualizations and data views they reference. --id takes one or more ids; --no-references exports only the dashboards. data is { space, count, exportDetails, objects }: the saved objects as Kibana exported them, and its closing summary (exportedCount, missingRefCount, missingReferences). Sent as a POST; it still only reads.
  • data-views list: List data views (id, name, index pattern). data is { space, count, dataViews }, each { id, name, pattern, namespaces }; a view with no name is named by its pattern.
  • rules list: List alerting rules with their schedule and last execution status. --search matches names; --page and --per-page as for dashboards list. Each rule is { id, name, ruleTypeId, consumer, enabled, muted, tags, interval, executionStatus, lastExecutionDate, lastRunOutcome, error, nextRun, updatedAt }.
  • rules get: Get one alerting rule, including its params and actions (--id required). data is the same summary plus params and actions.

status and dashboards export hand a 429 back at once; the other commands retry it.

toil kibana status
toil kibana spaces list
toil kibana dashboards list --search "payments*" --space ops
toil kibana dashboards export --id abc12345 abc12346 --no-references
toil kibana data-views list
toil kibana rules list --search "High*" --per-page 20
toil kibana rules get --id abc12345-0000-0000-0000-000000000000

Settings at a glance

  • baseUrl required

    Kibana root, e.g. https://kibana.imagile.dev (keep any context path, such as a basePath)

    TOIL_KIBANA_BASE_URL

  • apiKey secret

    API key: the encoded value; unset, a paired Elasticsearch connection's key is used

    TOIL_KIBANA_API_KEY

  • space

    Default space id for dashboards, data views and rules (unset: the default space)

    TOIL_KIBANA_SPACE

  • apiKeyFrom

    The elasticsearch connection to take apiKey from when this connection has none

    TOIL_KIBANA_API_KEY_FROM

Commands at a glance

  • toil kibanastatus

    Show Kibana version and overall status

    MCP kibana_status

  • toil kibanaspaces list

    List the spaces the API key can see

    MCP kibana_spaces_list

  • toil kibanadashboards list

    List dashboards (id, title, description, last updated)

    MCP kibana_dashboards_list--search <text>--page <n>--per-page <n>--space <id>

  • toil kibanadashboards export

    Export dashboards as saved objects, including the visualizations and data views

    MCP kibana_dashboards_export--id <ids...>--no-references--space <id>

  • toil kibanadata-views list

    List data views (id, name, index pattern)

    MCP kibana_data_views_list--space <id>

  • toil kibanarules list

    List alerting rules with their schedule and last execution status

    MCP kibana_rules_list--search <text>--page <n>--per-page <n>--space <id>

  • toil kibanarules get

    Get one alerting rule, including its params and actions

    MCP kibana_rules_get--id <id>--space <id>
